purpose: Present an edge task surface with optional source-supported swipe and snap-point behavior.
avoid: The depicted position does not establish modal semantics.
basis: Pinned React/primitive sources lead API, lifecycle and semantics; native visual observations and explicit reference decisions are mapped in figma/traceability.json.
profileRationale: The family presents controls or navigation; static depictions do not establish an interactive contract.
sourceRule: The wrapper defaults modal=true, swipeDirection=down and showSwipeHandle=false. Snap points are viewport fractions, pixels or px/rem strings as declared by the primitive. A snap-point change does not imply dismissal. Only a source-reported eligible swipe requests open=false; callback cancellation and controlled props still govern acceptance.
keyboardAndFocus: The default modal drawer contains focus, supports Escape/Close and restores the trigger focus. Pointer swipes use the configured direction and primitive gesture logic; keyboard access remains available through explicit controls.
referenceDecisions: One stable trigger/content ownership relation per shown instance; concrete labels and task children are caller supplied. Exact wrapper types retain optional handles/payloads/placement overrides. Complete describes this sufficient reference, not a full application/platform certification.

visualContract.layoutPolicy: The pinned Drawer wrapper owns the actual parts and primitive lifecycle; Root/Portal are controllers rather than invented DOM identities. The edge surface follows actual swipeDirection values; horizontal edge surfaces cap at the selected native 384px width, vertical edge surfaces span the available viewport. Header inset 16px/gap 2px and footer inset 20px/gap 8px retain native section metrics. Native title 16/24 (Medium, or Semi Bold for AlertDialog) and body 14/20 are intrinsic text roles, never fixed frame heights. Footer order remains DOM order and wraps. Button actions explicitly depend on Button tokens/CVA, while primitive triggers remain bare unless the caller composes Button. Backdrop 50% and viewport clearance are explicit reference decisions; static examples do not measure live dimming. Close and Escape follow the actual primitive callback and host authority; no CSS rule invents state transitions. The pinned Drawer motion utilities bind the documented live primitive swipe, measured height, snap offset and nested-stack variables. These are real runtime inputs, not DTCG observations. Upstream 450ms easing,400ms release scalar,16px stack peek,0.05 scale step and 96px vertical clearance are explicit source-code decisions. Reduced motion disables transitions without disabling gestures or closing. All lifecycle attributes remain primitive output, never new public state props.
